i18n.en: The oracle concerning Damascus. Behold, Damascus is taken away from being a city, and it shall be a ruinous heap.
i18n.he: מַשָּׂ֖א דַּמָּ֑שֶׂק הִנֵּ֤ה דַמֶּ֙שֶׂק֙ מוּסָ֣ר מֵעִ֔יר וְהָיְתָ֖ה מְעִ֥י מַפָּלָֽה׃

notes.official:
*Maśśāʾ dammāśeq* is “The oracle concerning Damascus,” the superscription formula of 13:1 and 15:1 (overlay `massa-oracle-superscription-isaiah`, extended here). ASV and JPS 1917 have “The burden of Damascus,” and NJPS has “The ‘Damascus’ Pronouncement.” The sense “burden” is reported in commentary only. “Damascus” is the city and “Aram” the state, as in chapters 7–9 (overlay `aram-names-isaiah`).

*Wᵉhāyᵉṯāh mᵉʿî mappālāh* “and it shall be a ruinous heap” follows ASV and JPS 1917 (NJPS “a heap of ruins”). *Mᵉʿî* occurs only here. It is usually explained as a by-form of *ʿî* “heap of ruins” (Mic 1:6; 3:12), and its sound repeats *mēʿîr* “from (being) a city” earlier in the verse. Emending to *lᵉʿî* “into a ruin,” or treating *mᵉʿî* as a dittography of *mēʿîr*, is a conjecture without manuscript support known to the editor, and it is not adopted. *Mûsār mēʿîr* “is taken away from being a city” follows ASV and JPS 1917 (NJPS “shall cease to be a city”).

i18n.he: עֲזֻב֖וֹת עָרֵ֣י עֲרֹעֵ֑ר לַעֲדָרִ֣ים תִּֽהְיֶ֔ינָה וְרָבְצ֖וּ וְאֵ֥ין מַחֲרִֽיד׃

notes.official:
*ʿĂzuḇôṯ ʿārê ʿărōʿēr* “The cities of Aroer are forsaken” follows MT, as do ASV, JPS 1917 and NJPS. Aroer is otherwise a town on the Arnon (Deut 2:36; Josh 13:9) or a town of Gad near Rabbah (Josh 13:25), so the name is unexpected in an oracle on Damascus. NJPS notes that an emendation, with support from the Septuagint, yields “Its towns shall be deserted forevermore,” reading *ʿăḏê ʿaḏ* “for ever” for *ʿārê ʿărōʿēr*. The Septuagint wording itself was not checked against an edition. The line keeps MT under the book's textual policy (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`).

The Hebrew separates the feminine *tihyeynāh* “they (the cities) shall be” from the masculine *wᵉrāḇᵉṣû* “and they (the flocks) shall lie down.” The line therefore renders the second verb as a relative clause, “which shall lie down,” with ASV and JPS 1917, so that the flocks, not the cities, lie down (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-17`). *Wᵉʾên maḥărîḏ* “and none shall make them afraid” is a stock phrase of secure rest (Lev 26:6; Mic 4:4). Here it describes flocks grazing where the towns stood.

paragraphs.text: וְנִשְׁבַּ֤ת מִבְצָר֙ מֵֽאֶפְרַ֔יִם וּמַמְלָכָ֥ה מִדַּמֶּ֖שֶׂק וּשְׁאָ֣ר אֲרָ֑ם כִּכְב֤וֹד בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ יִֽהְי֔וּ נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And the fortress shall cease from Ephraim, and the kingdom from Damascus, and the remnant of Aram; they shall be like the glory of the children of Israel, says YHWH of hosts.
i18n.he: וְנִשְׁבַּ֤ת מִבְצָר֙ מֵֽאֶפְרַ֔יִם וּמַמְלָכָ֥ה מִדַּמֶּ֖שֶׂק וּשְׁאָ֣ר אֲרָ֑ם כִּכְב֤וֹד בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ יִֽהְי֔וּ נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃ (ס)

notes.official:
The athnach falls on *ʾărām*, so the first half-verse closes with *ûšᵉʾār ʾărām* “and the remnant of Aram.” Read with the accents, the phrase either joins the list of what ceases, or stands fronted as the subject of what follows (“and the remnant of Aram: they shall be …”), since a disjunctive accent can also close a fronted subject. *Kiḵḇôḏ bᵉnê-yiśrāʾēl yihyû* “they shall be like the glory of the children of Israel” then follows as its own clause. The line follows ASV, and its semicolon allows both readings. JPS 1917 (“and the remnant of Aram shall be as the glory of the children of Israel”) and NJPS (“The remnant of Aram shall become like the mass of Israelites”) make the remnant of Aram the subject of the plural verb. On either construal, Aram's remnant will fare as Israel's glory fares in 17:4.

*Kāḇôḏ* is “glory” under the strict wave concordance, in this verse and the next. The comparison turns on the word's basic sense of weight and substance: NJPS renders it “mass” in both verses, and 17:4 develops it with the image of flesh growing lean. NJPS also records an emendation of “Ephraim” to “Aram” in the first clause; MT is kept (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`). *Nᵉʾum YHWH ṣᵉḇāʾôṯ* is “says YHWH of hosts” (overlay `yhwh-tzevaot-hosts-isaiah`).

paragraphs.translit: wənišbat mibṣār mēʾeprayim ūmamlākāh middammeśeq ūšəʾār ʾărām kikbōd bənē-yiśrāʾēl yihyū nəʾum YHWH ṣəbāʾōt (s)

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא יִדַּ֖ל כְּב֣וֹד יַעֲקֹ֑ב וּמִשְׁמַ֥ן בְּשָׂר֖וֹ יֵרָזֶֽה׃

i18n.en: And it shall come to pass in that day that the glory of Jacob shall be made thin, and the fatness of his flesh shall grow lean.
i18n.he: וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא יִדַּ֖ל כְּב֣וֹד יַעֲקֹ֑ב וּמִשְׁמַ֥ן בְּשָׂר֖וֹ יֵרָזֶֽה׃

notes.official: *Yiddal kᵉḇôḏ yaʿăqōḇ* “the glory of Jacob shall be made thin”: *dll* “be low, thin” and *rzh* “grow lean” describe a body losing its fat, so *kāḇôḏ* here carries its physical sense of weight. The line keeps “glory” under the wave concordance, with ASV and JPS 1917. NJPS reads “The mass of Jacob shall dwindle.”

paragraphs.translit: wəhāyāh bayyōm hahūʾ yiddal kəbōd yaʿăqōb ūmišman bəśārō yērāzeh

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָ֗ה כֶּֽאֱסֹף֙ קָצִ֣יר קָמָ֔ה וּזְרֹע֖וֹ שִׁבֳּלִ֣ים יִקְצ֑וֹר וְהָיָ֛ה כִּמְלַקֵּ֥ט שִׁבֳּלִ֖ים בְּעֵ֥מֶק רְפָאִֽים׃

i18n.en: And it shall be as when the harvester gathers the standing grain, and his arm reaps the ears; and it shall be as when one gleans ears in the valley of Rephaim.
i18n.he: וְהָיָ֗ה כֶּֽאֱסֹף֙ קָצִ֣יר קָמָ֔ה וּזְרֹע֖וֹ שִׁבֳּלִ֣ים יִקְצ֑וֹר וְהָיָ֛ה כִּמְלַקֵּ֥ט שִׁבֳּלִ֖ים בְּעֵ֥מֶק רְפָאִֽים׃

notes.official:
*Keʾĕsōp̄ qāṣîr qāmāh* “as when the harvester gathers the standing grain”: MT *qāṣîr* normally means “harvest,” and here it stands for the one who harvests. ASV and JPS 1917 have “the harvestman,” and NJPS has “the reaper.” Repointing to *qōṣēr* “reaper” gives the same sense and is not needed. *Ûzᵉrōʿô šibbŏlîm yiqṣôr* “and his arm reaps the ears” follows ASV (NJPS “who reaps ears by the armful”).

*ʿĒmeq rᵉp̄āʾîm* “the valley of Rephaim” is the place name near Jerusalem (Josh 15:8; 2 Sam 5:18, 22), and it is transliterated. The overlay `rephaim-shades-dead-isaiah-26` (“the shades”) and the central `refaim-giant-peoples` govern the common noun. Both are deliberately not applied to the place name (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-17`).

paragraphs.translit: wəhāyāh keʾĕsōp qāṣīr qāmāh ūzərōʿō šibbŏlīm yiqṣōr wəhāyāh kimlaqqēṭ šibbŏlīm bəʿēmeq rəpāʾīm

paragraphs.text: וְנִשְׁאַר־בּ֤וֹ עֽוֹלֵלֹת֙ כְּנֹ֣קֶף זַ֔יִת שְׁנַ֧יִם שְׁלֹשָׁ֛ה גַּרְגְּרִ֖ים בְּרֹ֣אשׁ אָמִ֑יר אַרְבָּעָ֣ה חֲמִשָּׁ֗ה בִּסְעִפֶ֙יהָ֙ פֹּֽרִיָּ֔ה נְאֻם־יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ (ס)

i18n.en: Yet gleanings shall be left in it, like the beating of an olive tree: two or three berries in the top of the uppermost bough, four or five in the branches of the fruitful tree, says YHWH, the God of Israel.
i18n.he: וְנִשְׁאַר־בּ֤וֹ עֽוֹלֵלֹת֙ כְּנֹ֣קֶף זַ֔יִת שְׁנַ֧יִם שְׁלֹשָׁ֛ה גַּרְגְּרִ֖ים בְּרֹ֣אשׁ אָמִ֑יר אַרְבָּעָ֣ה חֲמִשָּׁ֗ה בִּסְעִפֶ֙יהָ֙ פֹּֽרִיָּ֔ה נְאֻם־יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ (ס)

notes.official:
*Bisʿip̄ehā pōriyyāh* “in the branches of the fruitful tree”: literally “in its branches, the fruitful one.” A feminine suffix is followed by a feminine participle of *prh* “bear fruit” in apposition. NJPS gives the literal sense in a note (“on her boughs, the many-branched one”) and renders “on the boughs of the crown.” ASV adds “outmost” (“in the outmost branches of a fruitful tree”). The line follows JPS 1917, “in the branches of the fruitful tree.” *ʾĀmîr* “uppermost bough” recurs in 17:9.

*Kᵉnōqep̄ zayiṯ* “like the beating of an olive tree” and *ʿôlēlōṯ* “gleanings” are the harvest images of the stable 24:13, and the English follows that verse. *Nᵉʾum YHWH ʾĕlōhê yiśrāʾēl* is “says YHWH, the God of Israel” (overlay `elohei-yisrael-god-of-israel-isaiah-24`).

paragraphs.translit: wənišʾar-bō ʿōlēlōt kənōqep zayit šənayim šəlōšāh gargərīm bərōʾš ʾāmīr ʾarbāʿāh ḥămiššāh bisʿipēhā pōriyyāh nəʾum-YHWH ʾĕlōhē yiśrāʾēl (s)

paragraphs.text: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא יִשְׁעֶ֥ה הָאָדָ֖ם עַל־עֹשֵׂ֑הוּ וְעֵינָ֕יו אֶל־קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל תִּרְאֶֽינָה׃

i18n.en: In that day humankind shall look to their Maker, and their eyes shall regard the Holy One of Israel.
i18n.he: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא יִשְׁעֶ֥ה הָאָדָ֖ם עַל־עֹשֵׂ֑הוּ וְעֵינָ֕יו אֶל־קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל תִּרְאֶֽינָה׃

notes.official:
*Yišʿeh hāʾāḏām ʿal-ʿōśēhû* “humankind shall look to their Maker”: the articular *hāʾāḏām* is generic. Under the book's rule it is “humankind,” and its singular suffixes take English plural pronouns (overlay `adam-humankind-ish-man-isaiah`). ASV has “men … their Maker,” JPS 1917 “a man … his Maker,” and NJPS “men … their Maker.” The choice of “humankind” also follows the book's own echo: 17:7–8 reuses the idol vocabulary of 2:8 and 2:20 (“the work of their hands … what their fingers have made”; “In that day humankind shall cast away their idols”), where the book already prints “humankind.” The English word leans more universal than the Hebrew. The Hebrew does not say whether humanity at large is meant or the survivors of 17:4–6, and a narrower rendering, “people,” is possible.

*ʿŌśeh* “Maker” is the participle of *ʿśh* “make” (central `asah`; compare “your Maker” at 54:5). The next verse uses the same verb for the altars, “the work (*maʿăśēh*) of their hands,” and for what their fingers “have made” (*ʿāśû*). The English keeps “make” in both verses so that the contrast between the Maker and the things made stays visible. The two verbs are also kept distinct in both verses: *šʿh ʿal / ʾel* “look to” and *rʾh ʾel* “regard” (ASV “look unto … have respect to”; NJPS “turn to … look to”).

paragraphs.translit: bayyōm hahūʾ yišʿeh hāʾādām ʿal-ʿōśēhū wəʿēnāyw ʾel-qədōš yiśrāʾēl tirʾēnāh

paragraphs.text: וְלֹ֣א יִשְׁעֶ֔ה אֶל־הַֽמִּזְבְּח֖וֹת מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה יָדָ֑יו וַאֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשׂ֤וּ אֶצְבְּעֹתָיו֙ לֹ֣א יִרְאֶ֔ה וְהָאֲשֵׁרִ֖ים וְהָחַמָּנִֽים׃

i18n.en: And they shall not look to the altars, the work of their hands, and they shall not regard what their fingers have made, the Asherim and the sun-pillars.
i18n.he: וְלֹ֣א יִשְׁעֶ֔ה אֶל־הַֽמִּזְבְּח֖וֹת מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה יָדָ֑יו וַאֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשׂ֤וּ אֶצְבְּעֹתָיו֙ לֹ֣א יִרְאֶ֔ה וְהָאֲשֵׁרִ֖ים וְהָחַמָּנִֽים׃

notes.official:
*Wᵉhāʾăšērîm wᵉhāḥammānîm* “the Asherim and the sun-pillars” takes the wording fixed at 27:9, where the same pair is purged (overlay `asherim-chammanim-cult-purge-isaiah-27`, extended here). The *ʾăšērîm* are wooden cult poles associated with the goddess Asherah. Because the noun names the object and not the goddess, the central goddess entry is not applied. ASV and JPS 1917 have “the Asherim, or the sun-images.” NJPS has “sacred posts and incense stands” here, and “sacred post … incense altar” at 27:9. The meaning of *ḥammān* is disputed. It is often connected with *ḥammāh* “sun,” which gives “sun-images” and “sun-pillars.” It has also been connected with an altar or shrine named *ḥmn* in West Semitic inscriptions, which gives “incense altars” or “incense stands” (recalled, not verified).

*Hammizbᵉḥôṯ* is “the altars” (ASV). The central `mizbeach-olah`, which governs a first-mention note at Gen 8:20, is not cited.

paragraphs.translit: wəlōʾ yišʿeh ʾel-hammizbəḥōt maʿăśēh yādāyw waʾăšer ʿāśū ʾeṣbəʿōtāyw lōʾ yirʾeh wəhāʾăšērīm wəhāḥammānīm

paragraphs.text: בַּיּ֨וֹם הַה֜וּא יִהְי֣וּ ׀ עָרֵ֣י מָעֻזּ֗וֹ כַּעֲזוּבַ֤ת הַחֹ֙רֶשׁ֙ וְהָ֣אָמִ֔יר אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָזְב֔וּ מִפְּנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְהָיְתָ֖ה שְׁמָמָֽה׃

i18n.en: In that day their strong cities shall be like the forsaken places of the wood and of the mountain top, which they forsook before the children of Israel; and there shall be a desolation.
i18n.he: בַּיּ֨וֹם הַה֜וּא יִהְי֣וּ ׀ עָרֵ֣י מָעֻזּ֗וֹ כַּעֲזוּבַ֤ת הַחֹ֙רֶשׁ֙ וְהָ֣אָמִ֔יר אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָזְב֔וּ מִפְּנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְהָיְתָ֖ה שְׁמָמָֽה׃

notes.official:
*Kaʿăzûḇaṯ haḥōreš wᵉhāʾāmîr* “like the forsaken places of the wood and of the mountain top” follows MT, with ASV. The phrase is obscure. JPS 1917 has “after the manner of woods and lofty forests,” and NJPS transliterates the nouns as names, “the Horesh and the Amir.” NJPS notes that the Septuagint reads “the Amorites and the Hivites.” That reading suits the clause that follows, about those who left “before the children of Israel.” NRSV is recalled as adopting it (not verified). The line keeps MT (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`).

*ʾĀmîr* was “uppermost bough” in 17:6, and the line takes ASV's “mountain top” here, where the image moves from a tree to the landscape. The noun itself means only “top, summit”; “mountain” is ASV's addition from the context. KJV keeps the tree (“an uppermost branch”). The departure from concordance is recorded in the overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-17`.

*ʿĀrê māʿuzzô* “their strong cities”: the suffix is singular (“his,” JPS 1917), probably referring to Jacob of 17:4. ASV and NJPS have “their.” The noun *māʿôz* returns in *ṣûr māʿuzzēḵ* “the rock of your stronghold” in 17:10, and the two verses are linked by it (overlay `maoz-shalom-refuge-peace-isaiah-27`). *ʾĂšer ʿāzᵉḇû* is active, “which they forsook” (NJPS “abandoned”; ASV passive “which were forsaken”).

paragraphs.translit: bayyōm hahūʾ yihyū | ʿārē māʿuzzō kaʿăzūbat haḥōreš wəhāʾāmīr ʾăšer ʿāzəbū mippənē bənē yiśrāʾēl wəhāyətāh šəmāmāh

paragraphs.text: כִּ֤י שָׁכַ֙חַתְּ֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׁעֵ֔ךְ וְצ֥וּר מָעֻזֵּ֖ךְ לֹ֣א זָכָ֑רְתְּ עַל־כֵּ֗ן תִּטְּעִי֙ נִטְעֵ֣י נַעֲמָנִ֔ים וּזְמֹ֥רַת זָ֖ר תִּזְרָעֶֽנּוּ׃

i18n.en: For you have forgotten the God of your salvation, and have not remembered the rock of your stronghold; therefore you plant pleasant plants, and sow it with strange slips.
i18n.he: כִּ֤י שָׁכַ֙חַתְּ֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׁעֵ֔ךְ וְצ֥וּר מָעֻזֵּ֖ךְ לֹ֣א זָכָ֑רְתְּ עַל־כֵּ֗ן תִּטְּעִי֙ נִטְעֵ֣י נַעֲמָנִ֔ים וּזְמֹ֥רַת זָ֖ר תִּזְרָעֶֽנּוּ׃

notes.official:
*Niṭʿê naʿămānîm* “pleasant plants” follows ASV (JPS 1917 “plants of pleasantness”; NJPS “a delightful sapling”). The adjective *naʿămān* is from *nʿm* “be pleasant.” In *ûzᵉmōraṯ zār tizrāʿennû* “and sow it with strange slips,” *zᵉmōrāh* is a vine shoot or cutting and *zār* is “strange, foreign.” ASV has “strange slips” and JPS 1917 “slips of a stranger.” NJPS has “What you sow proves a disappointing slip,” and NRSV is recalled as “slips of an alien god” (not verified). NJPS notes that an emendation, followed by the Vulgate, yields “true” for “delightful” (cf. Jer 2:21); MT is kept (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`). The verb *zrʿ* is rendered literally, “sow” (ASV “settest”).

*ʾĔlōhê yišʿēḵ* “the God of your salvation” and *ṣûr māʿuzzēḵ* “the rock of your stronghold” are construct epithets (overlay `elohei-yisrael-god-of-israel-isaiah-24`). “Rock” is lower-case as a divine epithet, as at 26:4 and 44:8 (overlay `yah-tzur-olamim-everlasting-rock-isaiah-26`). ASV has “the rock of thy strength,” JPS 1917 “the Rock of thy stronghold,” and NJPS “the Rock who shelters you.” *Māʿôz* is “stronghold,” as at 27:5 (overlay `maoz-shalom-refuge-peace-isaiah-27`). The address is feminine singular, as often for a city or people, and is rendered “you.”

**Comparative note (history-of-religions reading, not adopted in the line).** Several modern commentators read *niṭʿê naʿămānîm* as “plantings of the Pleasant One.” They take *Naʿămān* as an epithet of Adonis, an inference from Ugaritic *nʿmn* “gracious” and the Arabic name of the anemone, and see here the “gardens of Adonis”: plantings forced into quick growth and left to wither in a rite of mourning for the god. This account of the scholarship is recalled from memory, and the editions (for example Wildberger or Blenkinsopp on 17:10) were not checked. The reading draws on 17:11, where the planting sprouts in a day and fails, and on the cult of Tammuz denounced at Ezek 8:14 (NJPS “bewailing Tammuz”). The Hebrew names no deity, and ASV, JPS 1917 and NJPS all render the word as an adjective. The comparative material is collected in the central `dumuzi-tammuz-adonis-dying-and-rising-vegetation-god-cross-corpus`, which is not applied here because the line names no god. Compare “the gardens that you have chosen” at 1:29.

paragraphs.translit: kī šākaḥatt ʾĕlōhē yišʿēk wəṣūr māʿuzzēk lōʾ zākārətt ʿal-kēn tiṭṭəʿī niṭʿē naʿămānīm ūzəmōrat zār tizrāʿennū

paragraphs.text: בְּי֤וֹם נִטְעֵךְ֙ תְּשַׂגְשֵׂ֔גִי וּבַבֹּ֖קֶר זַרְעֵ֣ךְ תַּפְרִ֑יחִי נֵ֥ד קָצִ֛יר בְּי֥וֹם נַחֲלָ֖ה וּכְאֵ֥ב אָנֽוּשׁ׃ (ס)

i18n.en: In the day of your planting you make it grow, and in the morning you make your seed blossom; but the harvest shall be a heap in the day of grief and of desperate sorrow.
i18n.he: בְּי֤וֹם נִטְעֵךְ֙ תְּשַׂגְשֵׂ֔גִי וּבַבֹּ֖קֶר זַרְעֵ֣ךְ תַּפְרִ֑יחִי נֵ֥ד קָצִ֛יר בְּי֥וֹם נַחֲלָ֖ה וּכְאֵ֥ב אָנֽוּשׁ׃ (ס)

notes.official:
*Tᵉśaḡśēḡî* “you make it grow”: the form occurs only here. It stands parallel to *taprîḥî* “you make (your seed) blossom,” and JPS 1917 (“thou didst make it to grow”) and KJV (“make thy plant to grow”) read it as “make grow.” NJPS (“you see it grow”) also takes the word as growth, though not as causative. ASV's “thou hedgest it in” derives the form from *śûḡ* “fence about.” The Translator's draft followed ASV. The line now follows the parallelism, JPS 1917 and KJV, and the sense of growth that NJPS shares (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-17`).

*Nēḏ qāṣîr* “the harvest shall be a heap”: as pointed, *nēḏ* is the noun “heap,” as in the waters that stood “as a heap” (Exod 15:8; Josh 3:13, 16; Ps 33:7; 78:13). KJV (“the harvest shall be a heap”) and JPS 1917 (“A heap of boughs”) follow the pointing. ASV (“the harvest fleeth away”) and NJPS (“the branches wither away”) take the word from the verb *nwd* “wander, flee,” whose perfect would normally be pointed *nāḏ*. The line keeps the Masoretic pointing (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`). JPS 1917 and NJPS take *qāṣîr* in its second sense, “bough” (cf. Ps 80:12; Job 14:9; recalled, not verified). The line keeps “harvest,” the sense the word has in 17:5.

*Bᵉyôm naḥălāh* “in the day of grief”: *naḥălāh* is spelled like the noun “inheritance,” but here it is read as the Niphal participle of *ḥlh* “be sick,” as in *makkāh naḥlāh* “a grievous wound” (Jer 14:17; Nah 3:19). This agrees with ASV and JPS 1917 “grief” and NJPS “sickness,” and it pairs with *kᵉʾēḇ ʾānûš* “desperate sorrow” (ASV; JPS 1917 “desperate pain”; NJPS “mortal agony”).

paragraphs.translit: bəyōm niṭʿēk təśagśēgī ūbabbōqer zarʿēk taprīḥī nēd qāṣīr bəyōm naḥălāh ūkəʾēb ʾānūš (s)

paragraphs.text: ה֗וֹי הֲמוֹן֙ עַמִּ֣ים רַבִּ֔ים כַּהֲמ֥וֹת יַמִּ֖ים יֶהֱמָי֑וּן וּשְׁא֣וֹן לְאֻמִּ֔ים כִּשְׁא֛וֹן מַ֥יִם כַּבִּירִ֖ים יִשָּׁאֽוּן׃

i18n.en: Woe, the uproar of many peoples, who roar like the roaring of the seas, and the rushing of nations, who rush like the rushing of mighty waters!
i18n.he: ה֗וֹי הֲמוֹן֙ עַמִּ֣ים רַבִּ֔ים כַּהֲמ֥וֹת יַמִּ֖ים יֶהֱמָי֑וּן וּשְׁא֣וֹן לְאֻמִּ֔ים כִּשְׁא֛וֹן מַ֥יִם כַּבִּירִ֖ים יִשָּׁאֽוּן׃

notes.official: *Hôy* is “Woe,” in the vocative construction “Woe, the uproar of many peoples” (overlay `hoy-woe-isaiah`; compare “Woe, Ariel,” 29:1). ASV, JPS 1917 and NJPS have “Ah,” and KJV has “Woe to.” The verse uses each of two roots three times: *hmh* (*hămôn … kahămôṯ … yehĕmāyûn*) and *šʾh* (*šᵉʾôn … kišʾôn … yiššāʾûn*). The line keeps both patterns with ASV: “uproar … roar … roaring” and “rushing … rush … rushing.” *Yammîm* “seas” is plural (ASV; NJPS “the sea”).

paragraphs.translit: hōy hămōn ʿammīm rabbīm kahămōt yammīm yehĕmāyūn ūšəʾōn ləʾummīm kišʾōn mayim kabbīrīm yiššāʾūn

paragraphs.text: לְאֻמִּ֗ים כִּשְׁא֞וֹן מַ֤יִם רַבִּים֙ יִשָּׁא֔וּן וְגָ֥עַר בּ֖וֹ וְנָ֣ס מִמֶּרְחָ֑ק וְרֻדַּ֗ף כְּמֹ֤ץ הָרִים֙ לִפְנֵי־ר֔וּחַ וּכְגַלְגַּ֖ל לִפְנֵ֥י סוּפָֽה׃

i18n.en: The nations rush like the rushing of many waters; but he shall rebuke them, and they shall flee far away, and shall be chased like the chaff of the mountains before the wind, and like whirling dust before the storm.
i18n.he: לְאֻמִּ֗ים כִּשְׁא֞וֹן מַ֤יִם רַבִּים֙ יִשָּׁא֔וּן וְגָ֥עַר בּ֖וֹ וְנָ֣ס מִמֶּרְחָ֑ק וְרֻדַּ֗ף כְּמֹ֤ץ הָרִים֙ לִפְנֵי־ר֔וּחַ וּכְגַלְגַּ֖ל לִפְנֵ֥י סוּפָֽה׃

notes.official:
*Ûḵᵉḡalgal lip̄nê sûp̄āh* “and like whirling dust before the storm” follows ASV and JPS 1917. *Galgal* is a wheel or anything that whirls; here it is the dry plant-head that rolls before the wind (NJPS “tumbleweed”; KJV “a rolling thing”). *Sûp̄āh* is printed “whirlwind” at 5:28 and 29:6. The line keeps ASV's “storm” here, to avoid “whirling … whirlwind” in one phrase, and records the departure in the overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-17`. NJPS has “gale.”

*Wᵉḡāʿar bô* “but he shall rebuke them”: the suffix is singular, treating the nations as a collective, and is rendered “them” with ASV. The Hebrew does not name the subject. KJV supplies “God” in italics, and NJPS has “He.”

paragraphs.translit: ləʾummīm kišʾōn mayim rabbīm yiššāʾūn wəgāʿar bō wənās mimmerḥāq wəruddap kəmōṣ hārīm lipnē-rūaḥ ūkəgalgal lipnē sūpāh

paragraphs.text: לְעֵ֥ת עֶ֙רֶב֙ וְהִנֵּ֣ה בַלָּהָ֔ה בְּטֶ֥רֶם בֹּ֖קֶר אֵינֶ֑נּוּ זֶ֚ה חֵ֣לֶק שׁוֹסֵ֔ינוּ וְגוֹרָ֖ל לְבֹזְזֵֽינוּ׃ (ס)

i18n.en: At evening time, behold, terror! Before morning they are no more. This is the portion of those who despoil us, and the lot of those who plunder us.
i18n.he: לְעֵ֥ת עֶ֙רֶב֙ וְהִנֵּ֣ה בַלָּהָ֔ה בְּטֶ֥רֶם בֹּ֖קֶר אֵינֶ֑נּוּ זֶ֚ה חֵ֣לֶק שׁוֹסֵ֔ינוּ וְגוֹרָ֖ל לְבֹזְזֵֽינוּ׃ (ס)

notes.official: *Bᵉṭerem bōqer ʾênennû* “before morning they are no more”: *ʾênennû* is singular (“he is not”), with the attacking host as a collective. ASV and JPS 1917 have “they are not,” and NJPS “it is no more.” *Šōsênû* “those who despoil us” follows ASV. *Ḇōzᵉzênû* “those who plunder us” keeps the book's “plunder” for *bzz* (10:2, 6; 13:16; 24:3), against ASV and JPS 1917 “rob.” *Ḥēleq* “portion” and *gôrāl* “lot” are the words for an allotted share.

paragraphs.translit: ləʿēt ʿereb wəhinnēh ballāhāh bəṭerem bōqer ʾēnennū zeh ḥēleq šōsēnū wəgōrāl ləbōzəzēnū (s)
